references.numbering_basis: Curve-driven Gothic world update — image order in that message
references.category: Radiograph / CT scan of a carved devotional figure showing internal armature
references.role: Reveal the hidden skeleton inside a sculpted mass: rods, dowels and joints running through a translucent body. Basis for an X-ray skeleton-inspection render mode and for the rule that the skeleton lives inside the rock.
references.historical_style_uncertainty: Appears to be a conservation imaging plate (numbered arrows mark dowels, nails, joints); object, collection, date and imaging method unverified. Figurative, not architectural.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Not a building; a figure whose outer carved surface hides a straight-rod internal armature joined at nodes.
analysis.spatial_composition: Four panels: full figure, head, chest, base — whole-to-detail inspection sequence.
analysis.material_characteristics: Translucent density map; denser elements (metal pins) brighter than wood/plaster mass.
analysis.rock_formation: Analogy only: mass accreted around a rigid internal frame.
analysis.structural_hierarchy: Long primary rods through the body, short secondary dowels at joints, pins at terminals.
analysis.scale: Human-figure scale; panels zoom to sub-detail.
analysis.silhouette: Soft draped outer envelope; hard straight members inside.
analysis.procedural_implications: Render skeleton members as bright additive lines visible through semi-transparent lithic mass; members never leave the mass envelope; annotate nodes/members in debug overlay.

references.numbering_basis: Curve-driven Gothic world update — image order in that message
references.category: Stacked contour-slice wireframe of a mass transitioning from grid to cells
references.role: Represent volumes as stacked section lines; show a porosity gradient where a regular grid dissolves into rounded cells along one axis.
references.historical_style_uncertainty: Graphic plate with partial text 'CHNITTWABE' (likely Schnittwabe), 'Roter Kanon 224' and CJK characters; author, process and data source unknown; likely digital.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Slab-like mass with ragged stepped top edge; interior lattice.
analysis.spatial_composition: Single frontal object, left-to-right gradient from orthogonal grid to cellular/bubble voids.
analysis.material_characteristics: Immaterial — luminous scan lines; reads as a measured section.
analysis.rock_formation: Cellular voids grow in size and roundness toward one edge, like porous stone or honeycomb weathering.
analysis.structural_hierarchy: Dense fine horizontal slices; a few stronger vertical seams subdivide the mass.
analysis.silhouette: Rectangular overall with stepped/eroded top and bubbled right edge.
analysis.atmosphere: Dark field, pale glowing lines, faint data annotations.
analysis.procedural_implications: (1) Contour-slice inspection mode: draw iso-lines of the lithic SDF at fixed height intervals. (2) Porosity as a field with a directional gradient parameter, not uniform noise. (3) Keep a regular structural lattice visible where porosity is low.

references.numbering_basis: Curve-driven Gothic world update — image order in that message
references.category: Inhabitable stone tower with orthogonal frame consumed by bulbous rock accretion
references.role: Primary reference for the skeleton-to-lithic transition: rectilinear slabs, piers and stairs on one side; layered bulbous rock masses fusing over the other side while floors and openings stay readable.
references.historical_style_uncertainty: Appears to be a contemporary speculative digital render; author unknown. Grass tufts are incidental — do not add vegetation.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Multi-storey tower of floor slabs, piers, cantilevered balconies and an external stair.
analysis.spatial_composition: Asymmetric: clean frame on the left, rock mass dominant on the right and top.
analysis.material_characteristics: Warm pale limestone; masonry coursing on frame; rock shows concentric layered rinds.
analysis.rock_formation: Rounded lobes with onion-like strata, cavities and perforations; accretes onto frame members and bridges between floors.
analysis.structural_hierarchy: Frame (slabs, piers) is primary; rock is secondary mass that never fully erases slab edges.
analysis.scale: Human figure at base — tower roughly 8–10 storeys.
analysis.silhouette: Rectilinear lower/left profile breaking into irregular eroded crown with circular void.
analysis.atmosphere: Neutral daylight on white background; inspection-like presentation.
analysis.procedural_implications: Directional accretion weight (side bias); protected negative-space volumes for floors, stairs and openings; lobe-based implicit surface with layered banding; per-structure rock coverage 0→1.

analysis.atmosphere: Night, warm white light on black.
analysis.procedural_implications: Render lathe/sweep members as ring stacks (cross-sections at intervals) in skeleton mode; expose section spacing as a display parameter.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Clustered pointed spires of different heights; no openings.
analysis.spatial_composition: Dense cluster with one leaning slab wall on the left.

analysis.structural_hierarchy: Tall central spires, lower flanking spires — hierarchical like pinnacle groups.
analysis.procedural_implications: Strata parameter: quantise the lithic SDF in height (layer thickness + per-layer inset/offset); spire intensity maps to taper rate along skeleton verticals.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Masonry tower with floor slabs, internal stair and doorways; walls perforated by large irregular voids.
analysis.spatial_composition: Frontal section; vertical circulation spine in the middle stays clear.
analysis.material_characteristics: Cut limestone coursing plus rounded layered rock concretions.
analysis.rock_formation: Lobed, concentric-layered masses clustered at edges of voids; erosion holes of many sizes.
analysis.structural_hierarchy: Floors and core are intact; erosion and accretion are confined to wall zones.
analysis.silhouette: Stepped rectangular outline broken by eroded edges.
analysis.procedural_implications: Subtractive erosion field masked by protected volumes (floors, circulation core, doorways); accretion concentrated on void rims (curvature-weighted); human-scale reference for slab spacing (~3–4 m).

analysis.architectural_morphology: Two raised blocks bridged at the top, carried on clustered legs; small free-standing piers.

analysis.silhouette: Boxy core with soft lumpy fringe and hanging drips.
analysis.procedural_implications: Accretion density weighted by edge proximity and a downward gravity bias; legs as stacked ring/blob sequences along skeleton members; keep flat faces partly clean (cohesion vs. roughness).

references.numbering_basis: Step 47 feedback — dry-stone arch reference
references.category: Dry-stone voussoir arch on a mountain ridge
references.role: Primary reference for lithic stacking: discrete rough stones without mortar; radial voussoirs on end around the arch, flat staggered courses in the piers and base, bigger stones low, gravel around the base.
references.historical_style_uncertainty: Contemporary photograph of a built dry-stone arch (round, not pointed); location and builder unverified. Use for stacking logic and stone character, not for Gothic proportion.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Free-standing near-semicircular arch springing from two thick rubble piers on a stone sill.
analysis.spatial_composition: Frontal frame; the opening frames a distant ridge; strong figure/ground.
analysis.material_characteristics: Weathered schist / gneiss / granite: grey, tan, rust and greenish tones; rough split faces; no mortar.
analysis.rock_formation: Each stone is a discrete faceted slab or block. Ring stones stand on end, long axis radial to the arch centre, thin edges outward; piers laid in rough horizontal courses with staggered joints; small gaps and shadows between stones.
analysis.structural_hierarchy: Large flat base/sill stones → coursed piers → voussoir ring; size decreases with height.
analysis.silhouette: Jagged outer extrados from protruding stone ends; clean inner intrados.
analysis.atmosphere: Bright alpine daylight, blue sky, hard shadows.
analysis.procedural_implications: Stones are placed one by one in slots along the skeleton path: thin axis along the path tangent (voussoirs on a curve, flat courses on a vertical pier), cross-section filled with staggered stones, size graded by height, small gap parameter, tilt jitter, separate faceted hulls, gravel scatter at ground contacts.

references.numbering_basis: Step 47 — World stage atmosphere reference
references.category: Photogrammetry point-cloud survey of a tree with annotated capture stations
references.role: Primary reference for the World stage 'scan' look: the built world shown as a dense point cloud on pure black, with survey stations (photo frames, dots, traverse lines, monospace metadata labels).
references.historical_style_uncertainty: Contemporary social-media image of a photogrammetry / survey visualisation; author and site unverified. Use only for rendering mood and annotation language, not for architecture.

analysis.architectural_morphology: Not architectural: a multi-stemmed tree and ground patch reconstructed as points.
analysis.spatial_composition: Subject centred and vertical; ground scan forms a ragged slab that dissolves into black; annotation frames scattered around and over the subject, linked by thin straight lines.
analysis.material_characteristics: Pale grey-white points carrying baked daylight shading; colour survives only where strong (lime moss on the ground, red survey paint on the trunk).
analysis.rock_formation: n/a — read as: surfaces become stochastic point samples; density thins toward the top and edges; stray floater points form a faint halo.
analysis.structural_hierarchy: Subject (dense) → ground patch (dense near base, sparse outward) → overlay (frames, lines, labels).
analysis.scale: Single tree (~8–12 m); labels and frames are screen-space and constant size.
analysis.silhouette: Soft, granular edges from point sampling; no hard outlines.
analysis.atmosphere: Nocturnal, forensic, archival: pure black void, no sky, data annotations as the only graphic language.
analysis.procedural_implications: Sample every stone surface by area into points (density per m²), bake simple lighting into point colour, desaturate toward scan grey, thin coverage with height and noise holes, scatter floaters along normals; ground as jittered-grid points with a ragged radial falloff and lichen/moss patches near bases; survey stations placed by golden-angle around the structures, each rendering a photograph of the solid model from its position, linked by a traverse, with procedural id/time/date/coordinate labels and red paint marks at their targets.
